title: Recognize relative limits from relative finality in a fixed-diagram join slice
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and joins and relative limit diagrams from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $q:X\to C$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories, $K$ a small simplicial set, and $s:\Delta^0\star K\to X$ an arbitrary cone, with $f=s|_K$. Define $X_{/f}$ by $(X_{/f})_m=\{a:\Delta^m\star K\to X\mid a|_K=f\}$, with operators induced on the first block, and define $C_{/qf}$ similarly. These are quasicategories and the induced map $q_f:X_{/f}\to C_{/qf}$ is an inner fibration. If the vertex $s$ is relatively final for $q_f$, meaning that
$$\operatorname{Map}_{X_{/f}}(t,s)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{C_{/qf}}(q_ft,q_fs)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence for every vertex $t$ of $X_{/f}$, then $s$ is a $q$-limit diagram in the mapping-square sense of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. No prior relative-limit hypothesis on $s$ or any other cone is assumed. Empty $K$ is allowed.

source.place: Definition 4.3.1.1 and Remark 4.3.1.2, printed p.261, dual relative-limit form; Proposition 2.1.2.1 for inner fibrations of join slices. Comparison to coherent mapping-square universality uses the natural sharp/fat join comparison. HA proof of Proposition B.1.6, condition (6), printed p.1473, uses the resulting equivalence. Primary HTT page and HA passage read 2026-10-17; shared archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical recognition theorem.

proof.text:
First verify the slice assertions. The join-slice theorem says that $X_{/f}$ and $C_{/qf}$ are quasicategories. To lift an inner horn $\Lambda_i^n\to X_{/f}$ over $\Delta^n\to C_{/qf}$, transpose to a map $\Lambda_i^n\star K\to X$ over $\Delta^n\star K\to C$. First use the inner-fibration property of $q$ to extend its restriction on the pure first block to $\Delta^n\to X$. Glue that filler to the prescribed map. The remaining inclusion is
$$(\Lambda_i^n\star K)\amalg_{\Lambda_i^n}\Delta^n\longrightarrow\Delta^n\star K.$$
It is inner anodyne by the right-anodyne pushout-join assertion, taking $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ as the second monomorphism (an inner horn is one of the right-anodyne generators). An inner fibration lifts inner anodyne maps: right lifting is preserved when the left map is pushed out, composed transfinitely, or retracted. Hence the glued lifting problem has a filler. Transposing back proves that $q_f$ is inner. This argument also works for empty $K$, when the remaining inclusion is the identity.

source.place: Preliminary slice fibrancy; join lifting as in Proposition 4.3.6.4 (018J), followed by the fixed-diagram comparison used in Proposition 7.1.6.13.

proof.text:
Put $T=\Delta^0\star K$, $A=\operatorname{Fun}(T,X)$, $B=\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)$, $A_C=\operatorname{Fun}(T,C)$ and $B_C=\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)$. Write $r_X:A\to B$ and $r_C:A_C\to B_C$ for restriction. Form
$$D=B\times_{B_C}A_C,\qquad \pi:D\to B,\qquad R:A\to D,\quad u\mapsto(u|_K,qu).$$
The left-cone restriction lemma gives that $r_X$ and $r_C$ are cocartesian fibrations, with cocartesian edges exactly those whose apex component is an equivalence. Its base-change clause, applied to $E=C$ and $h=\operatorname{Fun}(K,q):B\to B_C$, gives that $D$ is a quasicategory and $\pi$ is a cocartesian fibration. If an edge of $A$ is $r_X$-cocartesian, its apex component is an equivalence in $X$, so its image under $q$ is an equivalence in $C$ (apply $q$ to its inverse and the two triangle witnesses). The same criterion in $D$ therefore shows that $R$ preserves cocartesian edges. All these categories are quasicategories by the cited restriction lemma and functor-category closure.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13, last paragraph, applying Corollary 5.3.7.5 (02VW) and cocartesian base change (01UF).

proof.text:
The functor $R$ is an inner fibration even though $q$ need not be an isofibration. Indeed, transpose an inner-horn lifting problem for $R$ to a lifting problem for $q$. Its prescribed part is
$$(\Lambda_i^n\times T)\amalg_{\Lambda_i^n\times K}(\Delta^n\times K)\longrightarrow\Delta^n\times T.$$
This is the cartesian pushout-product of the inner horn with the degreewise injection $K\hookrightarrow T$, so it is inner anodyne by the cited pushout-product theorem. Its defining left lifting property against the inner fibration $q$ supplies precisely the filler for $R$. No equivalence-lifting hypothesis on $q$ has been introduced.

source.place: Inner-fibration check for the exponential corner; HTT Corollary 2.3.2.4, before the fiberwise-finality argument of Proposition 7.1.6.13.

proof.text: Let $A_f=A\times_B\{f\}$ and identify $D_f=D\times_B\{f\}$ with $A_C\times_{B_C}\{qf\}$. Let $P_f$ be the coherent cone category $(\Delta_K\downarrow f)$ and $P_{qf}$ its analogue in $C$. The dual of the join-slice/cocone comparison gives equivalences $X_{/f}\to P_f$ and $C_{/qf}\to P_{qf}$, natural under $q$. Here duality reverses the two blocks: $(\Delta^n\star K)^{\mathrm{op}}=K^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^n$ after reindexing the simplex, so the stated cocone comparison applies to $f^{\mathrm{op}}:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to X^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then is reversed. On the other hand the fixed-boundary clause of the join-cone calculus gives equivalences $A_f\to P_f$ and $D_f\to P_{qf}$, again natural under $q$. Both constructions send $s$ to the same coherent cone, obtained by precomposing $s$ with $K\times\Delta^1\to T$. Thus we have a commuting zigzag of functor equivalences between the functors $q_f$ and $R_f:A_f\to D_f$, with the specified vertices corresponding.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13, first comparison square; Example 4.6.6.8 (04J5). Existing natural sharp/fat and coherent-cone comparisons implement this square.

proof.text:
A commuting square of functor equivalences preserves and reflects the predicate that every incoming mapping-space map to a specified vertex is a weak equivalence. For objects in the image, its mapping-space comparison square has equivalences on the two horizontal sides by functor-equivalence invariance of mapping spaces, so the two vertical maps are weak equivalences simultaneously by two-out-of-three. Every other source object is equivalent to one in the image by a quasi-inverse; precomposing with that equivalence and its inverse gives inverse maps of incoming mapping spaces: the cited composition theorem identifies the two composites with precomposition by the identity, up to simplicial homotopy. Apply this argument along the zigzag in step 4. The assumed $q_f$-finality of $s$ therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{A_f}(u,s)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{D_f}(R_fu,R_fs)$$
a weak equivalence for every $u\in A_f$. This is a statement about all incoming spaces, not just endomorphisms of $s$.

source.place: Equivalence invariance in the first comparison square of Proposition 7.1.6.13; the mapping-space argument is written out here.

proof.text:
Apply the opposite-category dual of the cartesian-initial boundary-lifting lemma to $r_X:A\to B$, $\pi:D\to B$, and $R$. Its hypotheses are supplied by steps 2 and 3, and its fiberwise mapping hypothesis by step 5. For every $n\geq1$ and every $R$-lifting problem with upper map $a:\partial\Delta^n\to A$ whose last vertex is $s$, it yields a filler with both boundary and image fixed exactly. Under opposites, cocartesian edges become cartesian edges, the last vertex becomes the first, and incoming mapping spaces become outgoing ones. To compare the right-pinched models under this reversal, use the natural pinch equivalences to arrow spaces: degreewise order reversal identifies $U_{E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)$ with $U_E(y,x)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The realizations of a simplicial set and its opposite are homeomorphic by reversing barycentric coordinates on every simplex. Consequently reversal preserves weak homotopy equivalences, and the fiberwise hypothesis is unchanged. Applying the relative-final boundary criterion to the inner fibration $R$ now proves
$$\operatorname{Map}_A(t,s)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(Rt,Rs)$$
is a weak equivalence for every $t\in A$. No prior limit property or preservation of final objects by transport is needed.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13, last paragraph; opposite dual of Proposition 7.1.5.19(2) (02WU), then Corollary 7.1.5.17 (02WS).

proof.text:
Fix any $t:T\to X$; its boundary $t|_K$ is arbitrary. The definition of right-pinched mapping spaces and the degreewise pullback defining $D$ identify
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(Rt,Rs)=\operatorname{Map}_B(t|_K,f)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{B_C}(qt|_K,qf)}\operatorname{Map}_{A_C}(qt,qs).$$
This is an equality of simplicial sets: in each degree a map to the pullback is a pair of maps with identical image, and the constant-initial-face and final-vertex conditions hold coordinatewise. Since $r_C$ is an inner fibration, the inner-fibration mapping-space theorem says that the second factor's map to the base is a Kan fibration. The strict-pullback/path-pullback comparison theorem therefore identifies this strict pullback with the homotopy pullback of those same two mapping spaces. Its comparison inserts the constant path. Compose it with the equivalence from step 6. The resulting map from $\operatorname{Map}_A(t,s)$ is exactly the comparison to the path model in the mapping-square definition: its coordinates are restriction and postcomposition with $q$, and its path is constant because these commute strictly. Hence that square is a homotopy pullback for every $t$, which is precisely that $s$ is a $q$-limit diagram. For $K=\varnothing$, $B$ and $B_C$ are terminal, so this reduces to the assumed incoming mapping-space equivalences for $q$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13 combined with Proposition 7.1.6.19(2) (02X1); the strict-pullback and path-model comparison is made explicit.

proof_origin.place: Detailed realization of the proof of Proposition 7.1.6.13, with Proposition 7.1.6.19(2), the fixed-boundary sharp/fat comparisons, and explicit inner-fibration and path-model checks. Online references are not archived in literature/; WANTED in report.md.
